Context is taken verbatim from the introduction of arXiv:2607.21508v1, with every forward reference to the refutation removed. The rubric must not be able to tell this conjecture was about to fall. Known outcome: FALSE, refuted by two explicit 12-vertex line graphs found by an LLM in ~83 minutes. See judgment/calibration.yaml :: stanley-claw-free-s-positivity.
claim: Prove that whenever a graph G is claw-free, its chromatic symmetric function X_G expands with non-negative coefficients in the Schur function basis.
verbatim: If $G$ is claw-free, then $X_G({\bf x})$ is $s$-positive.
context:
Given a simple graph $G$ with vertices $V(G)=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, the chromatic symmetric function of $G$, denoted by $X_G({\bf x})$, is a symmetric function introduced by Stanley that generalizes the chromatic polynomial of a graph. There are important open questions about the chromatic symmetric function $X_G({\bf x})$ of a graph $G$. For instance, Stanley conjectured in \cite[Conjecture 1.4]{StChrom2} that $X_G({\bf x})$ expands positively in the Schur function basis (i.e. is $s$-positive) whenever $G$ is claw-free, that is, whenever $G$ has no copy of the claw graph $K_{1,3}$.

Stanley checked that the claw $K_{1,3}$ is not $s$-positive and verified this conjecture for co-bipartite graphs, which are complements of bipartite graphs. Gasharov proved it for claw-free incomparability graphs of posets. In fact, the symmetric functions in this case expand positively in the basis of elementary symmetric functions (i.e. are $e$-positive), a stronger fact conjectured by Stanley and Stembridge in 1993, reduced to the chordal case by Guay-Paquet in 2013, and verified by Hikita in 2024 via a probabilistic argument. See also another later proof by Griffin--Mellit--Romero--Weigl--Wen via operators on Macdonald polynomials. For the claw-free and chordal incomparability graph case, there are other proofs of $s$-positivity using representation theory of the symmetric group and traces of Hecke algebras. In contrast, Dahlberg--Foley--van Willigenburg and Fenn--Sommers found families of graphs avoiding claws in a different sense with non $e$-positive chromatic symmetric functions. Another piece of evidence for the conjecture is the proof of the real-rootedness of the independence polynomial of claw-free graphs by Chudnovsky and Seymour, which Stanley showed would be a corollary if the conjecture holds.

Adve--Robichaux--Yong used computational complexity arguments of coloring of claw-free graphs to reveal a tension between this conjecture and a related conjecture of Monical on saturated Newton polytopes. Namely, it is unlikely that both conjectures hold.
